explanation: A holy place for worship and offerings dedicated to God, usually a building where religious ceremonies and rituals are performed.
The innermost room of the temple, also known as the Most Holy Place, where God's presence was strongest. In Solomon's temple, this room contained the Ark of the Covenant.
A unit of length used in ancient Israel, corresponding to approximately 48 centimeters. Used in Ezekiel 41 to describe the dimensions of the temple and its structures.
Large, vertical support elements in architecture, often made of stone or wood. Pillars were used in the temple to support the roof and decorate the building.
The entrance to a room or a building. In Ezekiel 41 this refers to the entrances to the various rooms of the temple and the Holy Place.
Structures that surround and define a room or a building, often made of stone, wood, or brick. In Ezekiel 41 the thickness and height of the temple walls are described.
A structure where offerings and gifts are presented to God. In the temple the altar was the place for burnt offerings and other religious ceremonies.
Smaller rooms located around the main room of the temple, used for various purposes, such as storing offerings and equipment.
A prophet in the Old Testament who received visions from God, including detailed descriptions of a future temple in Jerusalem.
